handbookNote: Alabama Law Enforcement Agency (ALEA) Marine Patrol Division boating safety and licensing program (alea.gov/dps/marine-patrol) -- unlike most states in this project's boating rollout, Alabama does not rely purely on third-party NASBLA-approved vendor courses: ALEA's own Driver License Division administers a genuine state-run written/oral exam at its statewide Driver License Offices as one path to the required vessel "V" license endorsement, while also accepting completion of an approved course (ALEA's own free in-person "Boating Basics" course, U.S. Coast Guard Auxiliary, U.S. Power Squadron, or an approved online vendor such as BoaterExam.com, Boat-ed.com, or Recademics.com) as an exam-exempt alternative -- this hybrid structure and its age framework were independently confirmed by three sources: ALEA's own boat/vessel license requirements page (alea.gov/dps/driver-license/license-and-id-cards/boatvessel-license-requirements), ALEA's boating education and operator certification page (alea.gov/dps/marine-patrol/boating-education-and-operator-certificationlicense), and Boat-Ed's independent Alabama course page (boat-ed.com/alabama), all agreeing that no one under 12 may operate a motorized vessel at all, that 12-13 year-olds must hold a Vessel Learner License and be accompanied by someone 21 or older with a valid vessel license, and that independent operation is allowed at 14 once certified -- a birth-date-linked exemption (a person who was 40 or older on April 28, 1994, i.e. generally born on or before April 28, 1954) excuses older boaters from the written exam requirement, statewide licensing began July 17, 1997 under Alabama's Boating Safety Reform Act, and effective October 1, 2024 Alabama recognizes a nonresident's valid home-state boating certificate rather than requiring a separate Alabama credential -- exam-format convergence was directly confirmed on Boat-Ed's own Alabama course page: at least 70% on unit quizzes and at least 80% on the final exam, unlimited retake attempts, roughly 3-4 hours to complete, minimum enrollment age 12, and a $54.95 course price (plus a separate $5 application/$36.25 issuance fee if applying directly through an ALEA Driver License Office instead); exact current pass-rate/question-count figures for BoaterExam.com and Recademics.com were not independently re-verified against live vendor pages during this build due to access restrictions, so only Boat-Ed's directly confirmed numbers are asserted -- content is also grounded in real Alabama-specific detail verified against ALEA's own published boating rules and regulations (alea.gov/resources/laws/boating-rules-and-regulations): the general vessel-registration mandate and ALEA Marine Patrol's direct role registering pleasure boats and licensing operators, PFD/life-jacket requirements including the Performance Level 50/70/100/150 and Type I-V labeling systems, the under-8 mandatory PFD-wear rule, Type IV throwable-device requirements for vessels 16+ feet, personal watercraft rules (minimum operating age 14, mandatory PFDs for all riders, lanyard-type or self-circling engine cut-off requirements, and specific reckless-operation examples such as wake-jumping and cutting between a tow boat and a skier carrying a minimum $150 fine), a 0.08% BUI blood alcohol standard with an automatic vessel-license-suspension penalty for chemical-test refusal mirroring the state's implied-consent framework for motor vehicles, a 24-hour reportable-accident deadline for accidents involving a fatality, injury, or property damage exceeding $2,000, navigation light and 86-decibel exhaust-muffling requirements, an aircraft-interference prohibition, and references to the Boating Safety Act of 1959, Roberson/Archer Act of 1994, and Boating Safety Enhancement Act of 2001 -- plus universal NASBLA-aligned boating-safety fundamentals (Navigation Rules, the U.S. Aids to Navigation lateral and regulatory marking systems, PFD types, required federal equipment including fire extinguishers/ventilation/backfire flame arrestors/visual distress signals, cold-water immersion, trailering/launching, and towed water sports safety) applied to Alabama's genuinely distinct waterway geography spanning ALEA Marine Patrol's Northern District (Lake Guntersville, Wheeler Lake, and the Tennessee River), Central District (the Alabama River system, Lake Martin, and Lake Eufaula), and Southern District (Mobile Bay, Bon Secour Bay, and the Gulf of Mexico near Orange Beach and Gulf Shores), including Gulf Coast hurricane-season risk (June 1-November 30) and hydroelectric-dam hazard zones on the Tennessee and Coosa River reservoir systems -- price matches this project's Motorcycle-tier boating convention ($7.99), not a placeholder
